text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-The government wants to compile all information on the number of days and why workers are on sick leave in a new register. But the proposal is now being criticised by doctors and legal experts.
-The competition authority has approved of plans by Telenor and publishing house Schibsted to cooperate on the Internet.

-Nobody would be surprised if Sparebankgruppen were to drop its takeover bid for Fokus Bank today. The Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission yesterday asked the group of savings banks to consider withdrawing its offer to buy Fokus.
-After sidelining itself for nearly 22 weeks, Norway's central bank is again intervening on the foreign exchange market to keep the crown from fluctuating too much.

-The Njord oil production platform will be almost 30 percent more expensive than originally believed. Yesterday Norsk Hydro received a claim from Aker Stord, a unit of Aker Maritime ASA, for about one billion crowns for Aker's work on the platform.

-Forex traders fear that Kjell Magne Bondevik of the Christian People's Party or Johan Jaboksen of the Centre Party could be Norway's next prime minister after the election in September. Traders are worried that a centrist government would disrupt the Norwegian economy by overspending its oil wealth and this concern is making the crown more volatile than usual.
-The planned merger of the saw mills and board production of forestry group Norske Skog ASA and KS Hedalm Trelast will further strengthen Norske Skog's dominating role in Norwegian forestry.

-The board of Fokus Bank has welcomed yesterday's statement by the Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission, which asked Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 savings banks, to consider withdrawing its takeover bid for Fokus.
